q: Warm-up 1. What does the Yodh of a III-Yodh verb become in the 3 m.sg. perfect (e.g. ḥ-z-y)?
opts: It is kept as a consonant: ḥzay

q: Warm-up 3. What is the root of īdaʿ (he knew)?
opts: The initial ī comes from Yodh.

q: Warm-up 4. In ʾaytāw-hy 'bring him!', why is the suffix -hy used instead of -eh?
opts: It attaches to a word ending in a vowel (the imperative ʾaytāw).
Because it is a feminine object.
The rule is about the preceding vowel.

q: Warm-up 5. How do you say 'I saw' (ḥ-z-y, 1 c.sg.)?
opts: That is the imperfect, 'I will see'.

q: What is the Syriac imperfect (prefix conjugation) mainly used for?
opts: The future, and the subjunctive in purpose clauses after d-

q: The construction d- + imperfect corresponds to which Greek construction?
In the story, what does the king threaten to do to Yukhannan?
opts: Have him killed in the day of judgment
Send him back to the wilderness
That was the chief priest in Lesson 6.

q: What condition does the king set?
opts: If Yukhannan does not leave his land
If Yukhannan does not stop preaching
The condition is about leaving the land.
If Yukhannan does not worship him
If Yukhannan does not pay tribute

q: What is Yukhannan's stated purpose for coming?
opts: To speak the word of God to the world
He says he will not fear.
Peal imperfect 1 c.sg. of ʿ-b-d in a purpose clause: 'that I might do'
The ʾe- prefix marks the imperfect.
ʾe- here is the imperfect prefix.

q: Exercise 2. Which forms are the Peal imperfect of q-ṭ-l for 'he will kill, we will kill, I will kill, they (m.) will kill'?
opts: Correct: 3 m.sg. and 1 c.pl. look the same.
The king went out in order to see Yukhannan.
The king went out and saw Yukhannan.
d-neḥzē is purpose, not a past fact.
Yukhannan went out to see the king.
The king will go out and see Yukhannan.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: Lā neqṭūl malkā l-gabrā ṭābā.
opts: The king will not kill the good man.
The king did not kill the good man.
We will not kill the good king.
The good man will not kill the king.
